comparisonClass: Publicly documented programs proposing or demonstrating space-based machine-learning or data-center compute, plus the launch, spacecraft, communications, and industrial capabilities of their named legal entities or disclosed partners.
releaseRefreshProtocol: Repeat the named-program and regulatory search for every release. Preserve this dated version; a changed disclosure creates a new registry version and must not silently rewrite historical results.

scenarios.label: Generic orbital-compute reference
scenarios.boundary: Neutral reference and sensitivity surface; not a company design, forecast, or achieved system.

scenarios.label: Independent orbital-compute reference
scenarios.actorBoundary: Independent technical studies and public research programs
scenarios.boundary: Use only commensurable denominators or an explicit not-parameterizable reason; independent studies are cross-checks, not one synthetic trajectory.

scenarios.label: SpaceXAI — AI1 disclosed design
scenarios.actorBoundary: SpaceX/xAI; excludes Tesla and other affiliated legal entities
scenarios.boundary: Published vehicle specifications plus independently anchored missing cost, life, utilization, qualification, communications, and availability fields; no commissioned AI1 cluster is established.

scenarios.label: SpaceXAI — long-term targets plus favorable model assumptions
scenarios.actorBoundary: SpaceX/xAI; excludes Tesla unless the affiliate-hybrid track is named
scenarios.boundary: Deterministic target sensitivity only. Launch cost, vehicle efficiency, and annual deployment are targets; qualification, life, and utilization are favorable assumptions and never Monte Carlo priors.

scenarios.label: SpaceXAI — explicitly bounded affiliate hybrid
scenarios.actorBoundary: SpaceX/xAI plus separately identified Tesla or other legal-entity inputs under a disclosed relationship
scenarios.boundary: Eligible only where every affiliate input, legal relationship, transfer assumption, qualification gap, and availability uncertainty is explicit; never abbreviate to the SpaceXAI case.

simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic LEO, cislunar, and lunar architectures retain the neutral anchor set.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S39-S44 provide commensurable mass, thermal, launch, or cost-boundary checks, not a complete common LCO vector.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 mass and power fields are disclosed or derived; life, utilization, qualification, capex split, links, insurance, and availability remain independent assumptions.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: Company launch and mass-efficiency targets are combined only with visibly favorable model assumptions.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Tesla capabilities do not supply a commensurable orbital-compute cost vector or guaranteed resource transfer.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Payload mass, launch price, route, and annual deployment cadence.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Neutral transport route and launch-price sensitivities remain the baseline.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: Independent studies supply launch-price and spacecraft-mass markers only where denominators match.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 discloses vehicle efficiency but no achieved launch price or deployment cadence.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: 100 GW/year, 100 kW/t, V3/V4 payload, and no-more-than-USD185/kg are target arithmetic, not an operating trajectory.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: No affiliate contribution supplies a verified launch cadence or fleet-availability parameter.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Orbital vehicle power ratio, radiator boundary, and environmental performance.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Independent power and radiator sensitivities define the neutral surface.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S39-S43 provide comparable power and radiator studies at their stated temperatures and denominators.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 supplies 150 kW solar, 120 kW average compute, and 110 m2 radiator area but not thermal duty, temperature, mass, or cost.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: The aspiration inherits disclosed AI1 power fields; it publishes no separate thermal trajectory.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Tesla thermal experience is terrestrial and does not supply a space-qualified vehicle parameter.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Physical survival, economic obsolescence, qualification, and cohort reuse.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic cohort, radiation, life, and obsolescence sensitivities remain unchanged.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S32 supplies TPU radiation tests and an explicitly incomplete system-reliability boundary.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 publishes no achieved whole-spacecraft useful life, qualification multiplier, or compute availability.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: Seven-year life, 1.2 qualification, and 0.95 utilization are favorable assumptions, not company targets.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Affiliate terrestrial hardware life cannot be transferred to orbital service without qualification evidence.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Ground and crosslink service, latency, bandwidth, and availability.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic communications capex, service, and outage assumptions remain the baseline.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S32 reports an 800 Gbps demonstrated link against an approximately 10 Tbps design requirement.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 names Starlink laser links but does not disclose delivered bandwidth, link mass, service cost, or availability.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: No distinct long-run communications quantity maps to the simulation.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Affiliates add no commensurable orbital-link parameter.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Launched, commissioned, and operating capacity over time.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic deployment, commissioning, and endogenous reproduction trajectories remain the model result.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: No independent study supplies the complete commissioning and reproductive-capital state vector.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 is a vehicle specification; it does not establish factory throughput, launches, commissioning yield, or operating capacity.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: Up to 100 GW/year is shown only as an annual target marker; it is not inserted as an achieved trajectory.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Affiliate terrestrial production is not a guaranteed or space-qualified deployment flow.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Cluster geometry, operator interaction, and common-cause exposure.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S32 supplies the 81-node, 1 km-radius Suncatcher design point.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 publishes a 20 m by 70 m deployed envelope but no cluster spacing, shell, plane, or availability architecture.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: The FCC application supplies an up-to-one-million-satellite envelope, not an authorized or commissioned topology.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Affiliate capabilities do not determine constellation geometry.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Collision, breakup propagation, avoidance, removal, and multi-operator shell capacity.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic shell and node sensitivities remain the baseline and are not calibrated to one proposed constellation.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: S32 contributes a proposed compact cluster geometry but not a validated conjunction or debris kernel.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 vehicle dimensions constrain one geometric axis; cross-section, shielding mass, maneuver policy, reliability, and shell allocation are missing.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: The filed maximum and annual target are stress markers, not authorization, fleet stock, or collision probability.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: No affiliate parameter closes the missing orbital-risk vector.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Service, repair, recycling, replacement, and retirement architecture.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: Generic serviceability, circularity, and transport sensitivities remain the baseline.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: Independent servicing sources bound route and repair feasibility; S32 instead assumes redundant replacement.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: AI1 names modular upgrades but publishes no orbital repair yield, depot, spares, service cost, or retirement pathway.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: Seven-year life is an analyst-selected favorable assumption and supplies no repair performance.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Tesla service and recycling are terrestrial and cannot be counted without an explicit qualified-transfer model.

simulationCoverage.relevance: Lunar, asteroid, electronics, and import-dependent physical-closure cases connected to the stated roadmap.
simulationCoverage.genericBoundary: The ten-sector and integrated source networks remain explicit assumption-class generic models.
simulationCoverage.independentBoundary: No independent program publishes a complete source-grade-process-tool-fleet closure vector.
simulationCoverage.disclosedBoundary: SpaceXAI publishes no seed bill of material, source yields, parent-tool graph, recycling yields, or closure coefficients.
simulationCoverage.aspirationBoundary: Lunar manufacturing and asteroid mining are stated aspirations without commensurable production or closure parameters.
simulationCoverage.hybridBoundary: Tesla adjacency does not establish off-world recipes, qualification, autonomy, availability, or transfer rights.
